Tangram Rules

Fill an outline with the seven pieces.

The rules

The pieces
Two large triangles, a medium triangle, two small triangles, a square and a parallelogram - together they make a square. Each piece has its own black-and-white pattern.
Laying
Choose a piece below the outline, then tap where it should go: it snaps into the nearest place where it lies completely inside the outline and on no other piece. Tap a laid piece to pick it up again. No dragging is needed.
Turning
Turn 45° turns the piece in hand by an eighth of a turn; Flip mirrors it (this matters only for the parallelogram). Every outline of this set lies on a grid, so a piece turned by 45 or 135 degrees fits nowhere - turn it once more.
Levels
Easy: 20 outlines with many solutions; faint lines show one of them. Medium: 20 outlines without lines. Hard: 21 outlines with only one or a few solutions. The computer has checked every outline: the seven pieces fit it.
Outline only
29 new outlines: numbers, letters, animals, people, houses and boats. Only the outer line is drawn - no lines inside - and a piece stays where you tap it even if it does not fit or sticks out. Try until the whole outline is filled; every one has a solution checked by computer.
Hint
Hint lays one piece where the computer's solution has it; pieces in its way go back below the outline. Solved outlines get a tick in the list.

Example

The house: the two large triangles make the roof, the other five pieces fill the walls.
